description: refactor(backend): event subscriptions from the app container - singleton bus and handlers, no second BuildServiceProvider, hub shared by plain registration
notes:
Why: `AddEventSubscriptions` (ServiceCollectionExtenstions.cs:254-321) calls `services.BuildServiceProvider()` at :256 and subscribes 40 handler INSTANCES resolved from that throwaway root; every handler keeps that container's IServiceScopeFactory for the life of the process, so singletons inside handlers differ from the app's (board 4 symptom: LocalRealtimeHub without sockets; worked around by a closure-shared hub in LocalRealtimeServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:37-45). Facts: EventBus.cs stores handlers in a STATIC list (:11-12) and Publish (:23-32) never touches the provider; all 34 handlers inject only IServiceScopeFactory and do their work inside CreateScope(); IEventBus is AddScoped (Startup.cs:186) and handlers AddScoped (:201-247); Host.CreateDefaultBuilder validates scopes in Development, so resolving Scoped services from app.ApplicationServices would throw.
Do: (1) SprintRay.EventBus: make the handler list an instance field (tests build more than one host per process); keep the API (Publish/Subscribe/Unsubscribe); fix Unsubscribe to compare `typeof(T).Name` (today `nameof(T)` = "T", never matches; no callers, so delete Unsubscribe from the interface and class instead if you prefer - say which); keep Publish synchronous and exception-transparent (callers rely on it today). (2) Lifetimes: `AddSingleton<IEventBus, EventBus>()`, all 34 handlers `AddSingleton` (they hold only the scope factory). (3) Replace `AddEventSubscriptions(this IServiceCollection)` with `UseEventSubscriptions(this IApplicationBuilder app)` (same 40 Subscribe lines, bus from `app.ApplicationServices.GetRequiredService<IEventBus>()`), called from Startup.Configure right after `UseLocalRealtimeIfEnabled` (:235); delete the BuildServiceProvider at :256-257 and the `.AddEventSubscriptions()` call at Startup.cs:188. (4) Startup.cs:90-92 `ConfigureApiBehaviorOptions` builds a third container to get ILogService: resolve it from `context.HttpContext.RequestServices` inside the InvalidModelStateResponseFactory instead. (5) LocalRealtimeServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:37-45: replace the closure/lock with plain `services.AddSingleton<LocalRealtimeHub>()` (+ the existing publisher forward :46); update the comment. (6) Tests/LocalRealtime/LocalRealtimeRegistrationTests.cs:84-95 `Development_EveryProviderBuiltFromTheCollection_SharesOneHub` describes the two-container situation that no longer exists: rewrite it to assert that ONE provider built with `ValidateScopes = true, ValidateOnBuild = true` resolves the hub, the publisher and `IEventBus` without throwing (ralph-plan rule 10: adapt, do not keep a fossil). (7) Rename the two mis-named handler files to their class names (PrintListItemAddedAddToPlatformJobEH.cs -> PrintListItemPreprocessedAddToPlatformJobEH.cs; the file with the trailing space in its name -> without it) - git mv, no content change.
RED first (Tests/EventBus/EventBusWiringTests.cs, new): (a) `Subscribe_ResolvesHandlersFromTheGivenProvider_PublishReachesTheAppSingleton`: ServiceCollection with `AddSingleton<Marker>()`, a test event + a test handler (handler takes IServiceScopeFactory, opens a scope, records the Marker instance it sees), `AddSingleton<IEventBus, EventBus>()`, `AddSingleton<TestHandler>()`, provider built with `new ServiceProviderOptions { ValidateScopes = true, ValidateOnBuild = true }`; subscribe through the new UseEventSubscriptions path (or the same Subscribe call it makes), Publish, assert the Marker the handler saw is `ReferenceEquals` to `provider.GetRequiredService<Marker>()` and that a SECOND provider built from a copy of the collection does NOT receive the event (instance list, not static). (b) `AddEventHandlers_EveryHandlerResolvesFromAValidatedRoot`: `AddDomainServices`-free collection with only `AddEventHandlers()` + the scope factory the container provides + `AddSingleton<IEventBus, EventBus>()`; build with ValidateOnBuild and resolve each of the 34 handler types (reflection over the registrations) - RED today because they are Scoped and the bus is Scoped. Then GREEN.
Gate after merge: be-smoke + lab-pipeline logs stage prove the realtime path still reaches the hub through PlatformJobUpdatedUpdateAppSyncEH / PlatformJobChangedPostQueueMessageEH.
